repair.label: Roof Repair
repair.lead: A leaking roof does not always need a complete replacement. Roof King examines the affected roofing, explains what can be repaired and puts the recommended work in writing.

topics.label: Leaks & flashing
topics.title: Find where water is getting in
topics.description: A ceiling stain shows where water arrived, which may differ from where it entered. An inspection looks at roofing, flashing and penetrations before recommending a repair.
topics.detail: Tell us when the leak appears and which rooms are affected. Previous repair records can help the inspection.

topics.label: Shingle repairs
topics.title: Restore the affected roof areas
topics.description: Missing or damaged shingles need a review of the adjoining materials and the roof beneath them.
topics.detail: Ask about matching the existing color, replacing damaged underlayment and correcting flashing around the repair.

topics.label: Repair or replace
topics.title: Decide from the condition of the roof
topics.description: A limited repair and a complete replacement address different conditions. The amount of damage and the surrounding roof belong in that decision.
topics.detail: Ask us to explain the inspection findings alongside the proposed work, rather than decide from one missing shingle.

topics.label: After a storm
topics.title: Keep the damage record clear
topics.description: Share the approximate storm date, any new leaks and photographs taken safely from the ground.
topics.detail: Roof King can document observed damage and proposed repairs. Your insurer determines policy coverage.

guide.title: A repair should address the water entry point
guide.copy: Ask what failed, which materials need replacement and how the repair connects with the surrounding roof. Photographs can make that conversation much clearer.
guide.secondTitle: What to share before your visit
guide.secondCopy: Bring previous repair records, interior photographs and the dates you noticed leaks. Stay off the roof; the inspection is the time to check roof-level details.

replacement.label: Roof Replacement
replacement.lead: Plan a new roof around the condition of your home, the covering you prefer and the installation details that belong in your estimate.

topics.label: Existing roof
topics.title: Understand what needs replacing
topics.description: Discuss existing leaks, repairs and the roof’s age if known. An inspection helps establish the visible condition before recommending replacement.
topics.detail: Ask how concealed decking repairs found during tear-off will be photographed, priced and approved.

topics.label: Materials
topics.title: Choose a roof you want to live with
topics.description: Compare shingle profiles and colors or discuss a metal roof system. Review the exact product proposed.
topics.detail: Look at physical samples beside your siding, brick and trim before approving the final color.

topics.label: Installation
topics.title: Look beyond the visible roof covering
topics.description: Review removal, decking repairs, underlayment, flashing, roof edges and ventilation alongside the chosen covering.
topics.detail: Discuss access, delivery, protection of surrounding areas and cleanup before installation is scheduled.

topics.label: Price & coverage
topics.title: Understand the items behind the total
topics.description: Roof area, access, existing layers and material choices affect the work. Additional concealed repairs need their own approval.
topics.detail: Review manufacturer terms and workmanship coverage separately. Keep the named products and written estimate together.

guide.title: Build a roof system, not a shingle order
guide.copy: Underlayment, starter shingles, ridge products and ventilation need to suit the chosen installation. Review those parts with the field shingles.
guide.secondCopy: Discuss driveway access, deliveries, outdoor belongings and existing leaks. Confirm how progress and the completed work will be reviewed.

materials.label: Roofing Materials
materials.lead: Explore asphalt shingles and metal roofing by appearance, installation details and published specifications before choosing a roof covering.

topics.label: Asphalt shingles
topics.title: Compare genuine colors and specifications
topics.description: Our shingle library brings product images, color choices, classifications and warranty notes together.
topics.detail: Open the badges to understand the tests behind wind, impact and fire classifications. Read their qualifications alongside each rating.

topics.label: Metal roofing
topics.title: Compare the complete metal installation
topics.description: Discuss panel style, finish, fastening and flashing with the roof design in view.
topics.detail: Ask for documentation and physical samples for the exact system being proposed.

topics.label: Energy information
topics.title: Review the exact product and color
topics.description: Solar reflectance, thermal emittance and Solar Reflectance Index can differ by product, color and manufacturing location.
topics.detail: Published values do not establish a fixed saving on every home’s energy bill.

topics.label: Roof accessories
topics.title: Include the parts beneath the covering
topics.description: Review compatible starter materials, underlayment, ridge products and ventilation with the selected roof.
topics.detail: The Timberline HDZ page explains verified companion products and illustrates their role in the assembly.

guide.title: Choose with your whole exterior in view
guide.copy: Compare roof samples with siding, masonry and trim. Then review the roof shape and installation details with the team.
guide.secondCopy: A test classification, warranty term and general lifespan guide answer different questions. Read the notes and confirm documentation for the exact product.

gaf.label: GAF Roofing
gaf.lead: Explore GAF shingles, compatible accessories and installation by Roof King’s GAF Master Elite team.

topics.label: GAF shingles
topics.title: Find the profile and color for your home
topics.description: Compare Timberline and designer options using genuine color images and published specifications.
topics.detail: Review physical samples and the exact product documentation before making the final selection.

topics.label: Roof system
topics.title: Plan compatible components together
topics.description: Underlayment, starter shingles, ridge details and ventilation need to match the proposed roof system.
topics.detail: See verified companions on the Timberline HDZ page, then ask which components are included and why.

topics.label: Certification
topics.title: Check our manufacturer designation
topics.description: GAF’s contractor profile is an independent place to verify Roof King’s Master Elite designation.
topics.detail: Ask which manufacturer warranty is proposed for your particular installation.

topics.label: Installation
topics.title: Bring the products into a written estimate
topics.description: Review tear-off, decking repairs, flashing and the selected shingles and accessories before scheduling.
topics.detail: Workmanship coverage and manufacturer product coverage are separate; keep both sets of terms.

guide.title: The system belongs in the product conversation
guide.copy: Choose the shingle you like, then review the components around and beneath it. A single accessory is not a promise against every future roofing problem.
guide.secondCopy: Ask for the warranty name, required products and registration steps. Roof King’s written workmanship coverage is separate.

certification.label: GAF Master Elite Certification
certification.lead: Verify Roof King’s GAF designation and understand how installation, product selection and written warranty terms fit together.

topics.label: Verify designation
topics.title: Check GAF’s contractor directory
topics.description: Use the manufacturer’s contractor profile to verify Roof King & Restoration’s designation.
topics.detail: Review independent business details and customer sources while evaluating the installation team.

topics.label: Product choices
topics.title: Choose the roof as well as the contractor
topics.description: Compare the shingle profile, color and published specifications for your home.
topics.detail: Certification does not replace the decision about the actual roofing products being installed.

topics.label: Manufacturer terms
topics.title: Ask what your installation qualifies for
topics.description: Warranty eligibility depends on installed products, the roof system and the written terms.
topics.detail: Ask for the proposed coverage by name, including registration requirements and exclusions.

topics.label: Workmanship
topics.title: Keep installation coverage separate
topics.description: Roof King publishes five-year workmanship coverage. Manufacturer product terms describe different coverage.
topics.detail: Retain the written documents and ask how to report an installation concern after completion.

guide.title: Verify the team, then review the roof
guide.copy: A credential is useful evidence. Follow it with a review of the actual products, preparation and installation proposed for your property.
guide.secondCopy: Your estimate, product names, installation records and written coverage are the useful references for a future question.

metal.label: Metal Roofing
metal.lead: Explore metal roof styles and the installation details around panels, roof edges, penetrations and adjoining materials.

topics.label: Styles & finishes
topics.title: Compare the appearance on your home
topics.description: Discuss available panel styles, finishes and colors with the roof shape and surrounding materials in view.
topics.detail: Ask for physical samples and documentation for the system proposed.

topics.label: Installation details
topics.title: Plan seams, fastening and flashing
topics.description: Review the selected panel system and the details around chimneys, vents and edges.
topics.detail: Discuss removal and any decking repairs before the new covering is installed.

topics.label: Shingles or metal
topics.title: Compare complete roofing proposals
topics.description: Material choice changes both appearance and installation. Compare the named products and work included.
topics.detail: The shingle library is another way to explore styles, colors and published classifications.

topics.label: Care & coverage
topics.title: Keep the exact product instructions
topics.description: Maintenance and finish care depend on the chosen system. Ask for its current product documents.
topics.detail: Confirm workmanship coverage separately and retain both sets of terms.

guide.title: Metal roofing needs more than a color choice
guide.copy: Ask how the proposed system handles panel joints, penetrations and transitions. These details explain what the installation team will build.
guide.secondTitle: Compare with the exterior you already have
guide.secondCopy: Review samples beside siding, brick and trim. Consider the roof shape and adjoining materials before approving the selection.

storm.label: Storm Damage Restoration
storm.lead: After wind, hail or ice damage, start with an inspection and a clear record of the affected roofing and exterior materials.

topics.label: Hail damage
topics.title: Have suspected damage inspected
topics.description: Changes in shingles and surrounding metalwork can prompt an inspection. Ground photographs alone do not establish the extent of roof damage.
topics.detail: Share the storm date and new leaks. Ask for the findings and recommended repairs in writing.

topics.label: Wind damage
topics.title: Review missing or displaced materials
topics.description: Photograph visible changes from a safe ground-level position and keep clear of loose materials.
topics.detail: An inspection can review shingles, roof edges and related exterior damage before repairs are recommended.

topics.label: Ice damage
topics.title: Discuss roof-edge ice and water entry
topics.description: Tell our team where ice has formed and whether water is entering the home.
topics.detail: Stay off icy roofing and discuss the removal approach rather than striking roofing materials.

topics.label: Documentation
topics.title: Keep photographs and findings together
topics.description: Keep storm dates, photographs and previous roof records for the inspection.
topics.detail: Roof King can document construction findings. Your insurer determines policy coverage and claim decisions.

guide.title: Separate observations from repair recommendations
guide.copy: Ask what was found on the roof, siding and gutters, and why each repair is recommended. Not every visible mark calls for the same work.
guide.secondCopy: Dated photographs, estimates and completed-work documents help explain the construction work. They remain separate from an insurer’s coverage decision.

hail.label: Hail Damage Roof Repair
hail.lead: Arrange an inspection of suspected hail damage and understand the repairs recommended for the affected roof areas.

topics.label: Inspection
topics.title: Look beyond a ground-level photograph
topics.description: An inspection documents the condition of shingles and adjoining materials after a reported hailstorm.
topics.detail: Share the date, safely taken photographs and any new leaks to put the findings in context.

topics.label: Affected materials
topics.title: Review roofing and surrounding details
topics.description: Ask which materials were inspected and what was observed on each affected area.
topics.detail: The recommendation should identify the work proposed rather than simply describe the property as storm damaged.

topics.label: Repair or replace
topics.title: Decide after the inspection
topics.description: Damage location, existing materials and the surrounding roof belong in the repair discussion.
topics.detail: If replacement is recommended, compare products and installation details before agreeing to the work.

topics.label: Claim records
topics.title: Separate findings from coverage
topics.description: Keep inspection photographs and the roofing estimate with your property records.
topics.detail: Your insurer determines coverage; ask it about submission requirements and decisions.

guide.title: A classification is not a damage diagnosis
guide.copy: Impact classifications describe controlled product tests. They cannot establish whether your existing roof was damaged in a particular storm.
guide.secondTitle: Plan repairs after the findings are clear
guide.secondCopy: Ask which areas need work and how proposed materials will connect with the roof around them. Retain the recommendation with its photographs.

wind.label: Wind Damage Roof Repair
wind.lead: Have missing, loose or displaced roofing checked after high winds and review the repairs needed for the affected areas.

topics.label: Visible changes
topics.title: Start safely from the ground
topics.description: Photograph missing materials and roof-edge changes from a safe position. Keep clear of loose materials.
topics.detail: Share when the damage appeared and whether you have noticed new water entry.

topics.label: Roof inspection
topics.title: Check the surrounding details
topics.description: An inspection should consider adjoining shingles, flashing and edges as well as the visibly missing material.
topics.detail: Ask for photographs and an explanation of what can be repaired or needs further investigation.

topics.label: Replacement options
topics.title: Explore products if broader work is needed
topics.description: If roof condition calls for replacement, discuss the named covering and installation details.
topics.detail: Read wind classifications with their test explanations and warranty qualifications in the product library.

topics.label: Documentation
topics.title: Keep the storm and repair records
topics.description: Share dates, photographs and any previous repairs with the inspection team.
topics.detail: For a claim, ask the insurer what evidence it requires and how it determines coverage.

guide.title: Missing shingles begin the investigation
guide.copy: The adjoining roof needs consideration before repairs are chosen. Ask what was found around the damage and how new materials will be installed.
guide.secondTitle: Know what a wind rating describes
guide.secondCopy: A test classification and a warranty answer different questions. Neither is a promise that a roof cannot be damaged by wind.

ice.label: Ice Dam Removal
ice.lead: Discuss roof-edge ice buildup, water entry and any repairs needed after the immediate ice problem is addressed.

topics.label: Current buildup
topics.title: Describe the immediate problem
topics.description: Tell us where ice has formed and whether water is entering. Ground-level photographs can help describe it.
topics.detail: Avoid climbing onto icy roofing or chipping at roof materials. Discuss the removal approach with our team.

topics.label: Water entry
topics.title: Inspect affected roofing details
topics.description: Water stains and leaks need an assessment of roof edges and adjoining materials when they can be inspected.
topics.detail: Ask what was damaged, which repairs are proposed and what needs further investigation.

topics.label: Attic conditions
topics.title: Review insulation and ventilation together
topics.description: Discuss the existing attic conditions alongside the inspection of roof-edge problems.
topics.detail: Insulation or ventilation work should follow the actual findings rather than an assumption that one product fixes every winter concern.

topics.label: Repair records
topics.title: Retain inspection and repair details
topics.description: Keep photographs and notes about water entry or previous winter problems.
topics.detail: If you contact your insurer, ask about its evidence requirements; Roof King documents construction findings.

guide.title: Ice removal and repair are different decisions
guide.copy: Ask which work addresses the buildup and which addresses damaged covering, flashing or roof-edge details.
guide.secondTitle: Use the attic assessment to guide improvements
guide.secondCopy: Review actual insulation, ventilation and water concerns before agreeing to additional work.

claims.label: Storm Damage Documentation
claims.lead: Get clear photographs, inspection findings and a construction estimate to support conversations about reported storm damage.

topics.label: Damage record
topics.title: Start with dates and observations
topics.description: Keep the storm date, when you first noticed damage and safely taken photographs.
topics.detail: Share earlier repairs and new leaks so the construction inspection has the relevant history.

topics.label: Inspection findings
topics.title: Know what the contractor observed
topics.description: Ask for affected materials, locations and recommended work to be identified.
topics.detail: An inspection describes construction findings; it does not establish policy coverage.

topics.label: Written estimate
topics.title: Identify the actual repairs
topics.description: Review materials, preparation, flashing, installation and cleanup.
topics.detail: Ask how concealed repairs will be documented and approved.

topics.label: Your insurer
topics.title: Take coverage questions to the insurer
topics.description: Discuss claim submission and evidence requirements directly with your insurer.
topics.detail: Roof King cannot promise claim approval, claim value or payment of a deductible.

guide.title: Useful records explain actual repairs
guide.copy: Photographs and a written estimate should make the proposed construction understandable. Ask why each repair is recommended.
guide.secondCopy: Store inspection findings, the estimate, insurer correspondence and completed-work records in one place.

siding.label: Siding Services
siding.lead: Explore replacement siding and material choices that work with your home’s trim, roofing and exterior details.

topics.label: Replacement
topics.title: Review the existing wall covering
topics.description: Discuss worn or damaged siding, removal and preparation before choosing the new exterior.
topics.detail: Ask how concealed wall repairs will be documented if they become visible during removal.

topics.label: Material options
topics.title: Compare siding by material and profile
topics.description: Explore vinyl, engineered wood and fiber cement in our product library.
topics.detail: Look at texture, trim, care instructions and the exact product proposed as well as its color.

topics.label: Colors & trim
topics.title: Choose the exterior details together
topics.description: Coordinate horizontal or vertical profiles with corners, trim and accents.
topics.detail: Physical samples beside your roofing and masonry help you judge the final combination.

topics.label: Storm damage
topics.title: Inspect affected siding
topics.description: Loose, cracked or missing siding needs a review of adjoining materials as well as the visible damage.
topics.detail: Ask whether a section can be repaired or broader replacement should be considered.

guide.title: Trim belongs in the siding decision
guide.copy: Window surrounds, corners and transitions shape the finished exterior. Review those details with the main panel selection.
guide.secondTitle: Plan for what is behind the old siding
guide.secondCopy: Concealed wall damage may only become visible during removal. Agree on how findings and additional repairs will be approved.

siding-replacement.label: Siding Replacement
siding-replacement.lead: Plan new siding around wall condition, the material you prefer and the trim and flashing that finish the exterior.

topics.label: Wall condition
topics.title: Inspect before choosing the work
topics.description: Share loose panels, moisture concerns and previous repairs with the team.
topics.detail: Ask how removal and any concealed wall repairs will be documented.

topics.label: Choose materials
topics.title: Find the right siding profile
topics.description: Compare vinyl, engineered wood and fiber cement, including care requirements for the exact product.
topics.detail: Judge samples outdoors beside your roofing, masonry and trim.

topics.label: Trim & flashing
topics.title: Plan the whole wall appearance
topics.description: Window surrounds, corners and material transitions belong with the main panels.
topics.detail: Discuss fastening, flashing and finishing requirements for the selected product.

topics.label: Installation
topics.title: Prepare for removal and delivery
topics.description: Review access, deliveries and protection of surrounding areas before scheduling.
topics.detail: The estimate should identify products and preparation, with a way to approve additional work.

guide.title: New siding should feel coordinated
guide.copy: Plan trim widths, corners and accent profiles with the main siding, roof and masonry before ordering materials.
guide.secondCopy: A brand can offer many panels and finishes. Ask for the product line and specification, not just the manufacturer’s name.

siding-types.label: Siding Materials
siding-types.lead: Compare siding profiles, finishes and care across vinyl, engineered wood and fiber cement.

topics.label: Vinyl siding
topics.title: Explore Variform by Ply Gem
topics.description: Compare profiles and coordinated trim for the exact panel proposed.
topics.detail: Review samples and product documentation rather than assume every vinyl panel has the same specification.

topics.label: Engineered wood
topics.title: Explore LP SmartSide
topics.description: Review the selected profile, texture and finish in the LP SmartSide family.
topics.detail: Discuss installation clearances, flashing, fastening and care with the team.

topics.label: Fiber cement
topics.title: Explore James Hardie
topics.description: Compare the exact fiber cement product, texture and finish alongside coordinated trim.
topics.detail: Ask for installation and care instructions for the chosen product.

topics.label: Plan replacement
topics.title: Name the products in the estimate
topics.description: Identify panel, profile, color, trim and wall preparation before agreeing to work.
topics.detail: Concealed damage found during removal needs its own repair and approval discussion.

guide.title: Include care in the material decision
guide.copy: Review cleaning, painting and finishing instructions for the exact product. Choose the upkeep you are comfortable with.
guide.secondTitle: Look at the full exterior palette
guide.secondCopy: Compare samples outdoors with roofing, masonry, doors and trim before approving the combination.

gutters.label: Gutter Services
gutters.lead: Plan gutters and downspouts around roof drainage, existing gutter condition and the route water takes away from your home.

topics.label: Drainage layout
topics.title: Show us where water overflows
topics.description: Review gutters, outlets and downspouts before choosing replacement materials.
topics.detail: Discuss proposed sizes, fastening and discharge arrangements alongside the problems you have noticed.

topics.label: Seamless gutters
topics.title: Plan the roofline details
topics.description: A seamless installation still needs clear corners, outlet and downspout connections.
topics.detail: Review fascia condition and any repairs required before the gutters attach.

topics.label: Gutter guards
topics.title: Compare protection with the system
topics.description: Guards and continuous hangers have different functions. Review the exact product and its compatibility.
topics.detail: Protection does not correct damaged or undersized gutters. Ask about cleaning and inspection.

topics.label: Roof edges
topics.title: Include adjoining repairs
topics.description: Gutter work connects with fascia and roofing details. Discuss damage in those areas as part of the proposal.
topics.detail: If roof repairs are also needed, ask how the work will be coordinated.

guide.title: Follow the water through the estimate
guide.copy: Discuss where water enters the gutters, how it reaches downspouts and where it is discharged. The proposal should explain that route.
guide.secondCopy: Inspect condition, slope and outlets first. Then compare a named guard or hanger system and its maintenance instructions.

guards.label: Gutter Guards
guards.lead: Compare gutter protection and support systems with the condition and drainage capacity of the gutters on your home.

topics.label: Existing gutters
topics.title: Check before adding protection
topics.description: Review gutter condition, slope, outlets and downspout drainage before selecting a guard.
topics.detail: Discuss overflow, loose sections and fascia damage before fitting a new product.

topics.label: Alu-Rex & T-Rex
topics.title: Understand continuous support
topics.description: T-Rex is an Alu-Rex continuous hanger system that supports gutters and screens debris.
topics.detail: It differs from Trex decking. Confirm the exact model and installation requirements.

topics.label: LeafFilter
topics.title: Review the proposed protection
topics.description: LeafFilter uses micromesh screening. Discuss preparation of the existing gutters before installation.
topics.detail: Confirm current product availability and who will supply and install the system.

topics.label: Care & coverage
topics.title: Keep maintenance in the decision
topics.description: Ask for cleaning and inspection instructions and the written product warranty.
topics.detail: A general maintenance-free promise should not replace the selected product’s instructions.

guide.title: Choose by function as well as brand
guide.copy: Screening debris and supporting the gutter are different jobs. Ask what the proposed system does and how it fits your roof edge.
guide.secondCopy: A guard should not hide an existing gutter problem. Identify cleaning, repairs or replacement before fitting protection.

seamless.label: Seamless Gutters
seamless.lead: Plan gutters, corners, outlets and downspouts as one drainage system, with fascia checked before installation.

topics.label: Current drainage
topics.title: Point out existing problems
topics.description: Show overflowing areas, loose sections and leaking connections from the ground.
topics.detail: An inspection helps establish what needs replacement and which adjoining areas need repair.

topics.label: Gutter layout
topics.title: Review sizes and outlets
topics.description: Ask for lengths, corners, sizes and outlet positions in the estimate.
topics.detail: Discuss how fascia repairs will be identified and approved if needed.

topics.label: Downspouts
topics.title: Plan where the water goes
topics.description: Review downspout positions and discharge arrangements with the team.
topics.detail: Existing connections and access need consideration alongside the new gutters.

topics.label: Protection
topics.title: Compare compatible options
topics.description: Once drainage is established, consider protection or continuous support if appropriate.
topics.detail: Choose a named product and review compatibility, cleaning instructions and coverage.

guide.title: Downspouts belong in the installation plan
guide.copy: Walk through the proposed outlet and downspout locations before work begins. Gutters collect the water; the rest of the system must take it onward.
guide.secondCopy: Loose or damaged fascia needs a repair discussion. Ask how that work will be documented and approved.

decks.label: Deck Services
decks.lead: Explore installation, replacement, repairs and refinishing with boards, framing, stairs and railings considered together.

topics.label: New decks
topics.title: Plan how you want to use the space
topics.description: Discuss layout, doors, seating, access and stairs before choosing boards and colors.
topics.detail: The surface is one part of the deck; supports and connections need their own review.

topics.label: Replacement
topics.title: Assess what can remain
topics.description: Have an existing deck assessed before new boards are proposed.
topics.detail: Ask which framing, supports and connections can remain and which need replacement.

topics.label: Repair & refinish
topics.title: Match the service to the condition
topics.description: Damaged components need a repair discussion. Refinishing concerns the surface appearance.
topics.detail: Ask whether repairs should happen before cleaning or finishing.

topics.label: Materials & details
topics.title: Coordinate boards and accessories
topics.description: Explore decking materials with railings, stairs and the products around the main surface.
topics.detail: Compare samples, compatible fasteners and care instructions for the selected products.

guide.title: Start with everyday use
guide.copy: Seating, dining, doors and access to the yard affect the layout. Discuss those needs before narrowing colors and textures.
guide.secondCopy: New boards alone do not establish that an older deck is sound. Ask what was inspected beneath the finished surface.

deck-install.label: Deck Installation
deck-install.lead: Plan the layout, structure, decking and access for an outdoor space that suits how you use your home.

topics.label: Layout
topics.title: Work out shape and access
topics.description: Discuss doors, furniture, stairs and the route into the yard together.
topics.detail: Bring a sketch or photographs showing how you want to use the space.

topics.label: Structure
topics.title: Include supports and connections
topics.description: Ask how the proposed structure and connections will be planned for the layout.
topics.detail: Discuss site preparation and any approval or inspection requirements for your project.

topics.label: Decking
topics.title: Compare boards and finishes
topics.description: Look at material samples and the care instructions for the exact decking.
topics.detail: Our Trex overview introduces composite boards and compatible products.

topics.label: Finishing details
topics.title: Plan stairs and rails with the deck
topics.description: Railings, stair positions and adjoining details affect both appearance and use.
topics.detail: Have selected products and installation details identified in the estimate.

guide.title: Design for the way you use the yard
guide.copy: The board pattern should follow a practical layout for doors, seating and yard access. Review those decisions together.
guide.secondCopy: Confirm boards, rails, stairs and finishes. Retain the product and care documents after completion.

deck-replace.label: Deck Replacement
deck-replace.lead: Assess the existing deck and plan replacement boards, framing, stairs and rails around the work actually needed.

topics.label: Existing deck
topics.title: Assess before resurfacing
topics.description: Review framing, supports, connections and boards before deciding what can remain.
topics.detail: New surface boards do not establish that the supporting structure is sound.

topics.label: New layout
topics.title: Ask whether the layout still works
topics.description: Replacement is an opportunity to review doors, stairs and how you use the space.
topics.detail: Discuss whether the new deck keeps the existing footprint or changes the layout.

topics.label: Materials
topics.title: Choose replacement decking
topics.description: Compare boards, color, texture and care requirements for the exact product.
topics.detail: Discuss compatible fasteners and the effect of the product choice on framing requirements.

topics.label: Rails & stairs
topics.title: Include adjoining features
topics.description: Review railings and stairs alongside the new surface.
topics.detail: Have removal, retained components and new installation identified separately.

guide.title: Replacement can change more than boards
guide.copy: Consider whether the current layout still suits your home before new material is ordered.
guide.secondTitle: Name what stays and what is new
guide.secondCopy: Distinguish retained framing, new structural work and replacement surface materials in the estimate.

deck-repair.label: Deck Repair
deck-repair.lead: Have damaged boards, loose components and concerns about an existing deck inspected before choosing repairs or replacement.

topics.label: Deck condition
topics.title: Show us the areas of concern
topics.description: Point out damaged boards, loose rails and changes you have noticed.
topics.detail: Avoid an area you believe unsafe and arrange an inspection of the affected parts.

topics.label: Repair work
topics.title: Identify the affected components
topics.description: Ask which boards, connections or other components need repair.
topics.detail: The estimate should name the actual work rather than simply call it a deck repair.

topics.label: Replacement
topics.title: Discuss broader work if needed
topics.description: Compare a replacement recommendation with the repair findings.
topics.detail: Review structure, surface, stairs and railings as separate parts of the decision.

topics.label: Surface care
topics.title: Refinish after necessary repairs
topics.description: Refinishing changes the surface appearance; it does not repair damaged components.
topics.detail: Ask what repairs and preparation should precede any new finish.

guide.title: Locate the actual repair in the proposal
guide.copy: Photographs and clear component names help explain what needs attention and why.
guide.secondTitle: Keep finishing in the right order
guide.secondCopy: Discuss repairs before cleaning and coating. A fresh surface should not conceal an unresolved problem.

deck-refinish.label: Deck Refinishing
deck-refinish.lead: Refresh an existing deck surface after reviewing its material, previous coating and any repairs needed before finishing.

topics.label: Existing surface
topics.title: Identify the deck and coating
topics.description: Share the deck material and previous finishes if known.
topics.detail: Preparation and suitable products depend on the surface already there.

topics.label: Repairs first
topics.title: Address damage before finishing
topics.description: Loose or damaged parts need their own repair discussion.
topics.detail: Agree on repairs before cleaning or applying a finish.

topics.label: Preparation
topics.title: Discuss cleaning and preparation
topics.description: Ask what surface preparation is recommended for the material and existing coating.
topics.detail: Review protection of surrounding areas and application instructions.

topics.label: Finish & care
topics.title: Choose with maintenance in mind
topics.description: Compare the proposed color, finish and care instructions.
topics.detail: Ask when the surface can return to use and how it should be maintained.

guide.title: Let the existing surface guide the work
guide.copy: Review previous coatings and the deck material before choosing a new finish. Preparation should fit the actual surface.
guide.secondCopy: Discuss color and the variation in existing boards rather than expecting older decking to look like new construction.

deck-accessories.label: Deck Accessories
deck-accessories.lead: Coordinate stairs, rails and finishing details with the existing deck structure or a planned installation.

topics.label: Railings
topics.title: Choose rails with the layout
topics.description: Review appearance, attachment and compatibility with the proposed deck.
topics.detail: Ask which existing components need checking before new rails are attached.

topics.label: Stairs & access
topics.title: Plan the route to the yard
topics.description: Stair location affects how the deck works every day.
topics.detail: Discuss adjoining work rather than choose an accessory in isolation.

topics.label: Products
topics.title: Coordinate the selected details
topics.description: Compare boards, rails and trim using samples and product documentation.
topics.detail: Confirm the exact compatible products proposed with Trex or another selected material.

topics.label: Existing decks
topics.title: Check what the addition attaches to
topics.description: Adding an accessory begins with the condition of the components supporting it.
topics.detail: Agree on needed repairs before the new installation.

guide.title: Choose details as a coordinated set
guide.copy: Review the board, railing and trim combination before ordering, including colors and profiles.
guide.secondCopy: A new accessory needs a suitable attachment point. Discuss existing conditions and any required repairs.

insulation.label: Attic Insulation
insulation.lead: Review attic insulation alongside existing ventilation, air movement and any roofing concerns.

topics.label: Existing attic
topics.title: Begin with the conditions in your home
topics.description: Share uncomfortable rooms, previous insulation work and any water entry. An inspection establishes the existing material and areas needing attention.

topics.label: Installation
topics.title: Name the material and treated areas
topics.description: Ask for the proposed material, preparation and access in writing. Existing conditions may need attention before insulation is added.

topics.label: Roof & ventilation
topics.title: Consider the attic and roof together
topics.description: An unresolved leak needs a separate repair discussion. Ask how the roof and attic findings relate before choosing improvements.

topics.label: Winter concerns
topics.title: Share roof-edge ice problems
topics.description: Tell us where and when ice forms. Discuss both the immediate problem and the conditions identified in the attic.

guide.title: Choose from an attic assessment
guide.copy: Ask what the inspection found and why the proposed work addresses those conditions.
guide.secondCopy: Insulation does not establish a fixed utility saving for every home. Discuss your rooms, existing material and actual installation.

windows.label: Window Replacement
windows.lead: Plan replacement windows around openings, operating styles, appearance and installation at each window.

topics.label: Existing windows
topics.title: Identify what needs attention
topics.description: Share drafts, difficult operation, damaged frames and water concerns before selecting replacement products.

topics.label: Styles
topics.title: Choose for the room and exterior
topics.description: Discuss operating style, frame color and the look beside siding and trim. Ask for exact products and sizes.

topics.label: Installation
topics.title: Review each opening
topics.description: Ask about removal, preparation, flashing and finishing. Agree on how repairs discovered during removal will be approved.

topics.label: Performance & care
topics.title: Read the product documentation
topics.description: Review performance information, care and coverage for the selected window. Ratings do not establish fixed utility savings.

guide.title: Choose windows and trim together
guide.copy: Review style, frame color and trim with the existing interior and exterior finishes.
guide.secondCopy: Openings can require different preparation. Identify the finishing and repairs included in the estimate.

painting.label: Exterior Painting
painting.lead: Plan exterior repainting around the existing siding and trim, preparation and the coating proposed for each surface.

topics.label: Surfaces
topics.title: Review what will be painted
topics.description: Identify siding, trim and soffit included in the project. Share peeling coatings, previous finishes and visible damage.

topics.label: Preparation
topics.title: Include cleaning and repairs
topics.description: Review preparation before painting begins. Damaged siding or trim may need repair rather than another coating.

topics.label: Color & finish
topics.title: Choose for the actual surface
topics.description: Compare coating, colors and finish beside roofing, masonry and trim. Discuss application instructions and scheduling.

topics.label: Completion
topics.title: Retain the product information
topics.description: Agree on the surfaces to be completed and final review. Keep coating and color information for later care.

guide.title: Preparation belongs in the color decision
guide.copy: Review damaged areas, old coatings and repairs before selecting the final finish.
guide.secondCopy: Exact coating and color information makes later care and touch-ups easier to discuss.

commercial.label: Commercial Roofing
commercial.lead: Plan roof repair, replacement and drainage around your building’s condition, access and day-to-day operations.

topics.label: Roof repair
topics.title: Investigate the affected areas
topics.description: Share leak locations, timing and previous repairs. Coordinate roof access and occupied areas with the property contact.

topics.label: Replacement
topics.title: Plan the roofing work
topics.description: Review preparation, the named roof system, flashing and drainage. Discuss deliveries, occupants and cleanup before scheduling.

topics.label: Roof types
topics.title: Consider the actual roof design
topics.description: Discuss slope, existing construction and installation requirements. Ask for the exact proposed system and its documentation.

topics.label: Drainage
topics.title: Follow the water off the roof
topics.description: Review gutters, outlets and downspouts. Include existing drainage problems and repairs to attachment areas.

guide.title: Coordinate with the building’s use
guide.copy: Discuss occupied areas, deliveries and access restrictions before work is scheduled. Agree on the property contact for communication.
guide.secondCopy: A broad material description is not a product specification. Ask for proposed products, installation details and coverage.

commercial-repair.label: Commercial Roof Repair
commercial-repair.lead: Investigate leaks and damaged areas with the building’s existing roof system, access and operations in view.

topics.label: Leak history
topics.title: Bring the roof records
topics.description: Share leak timing, locations and previous repairs. These details help focus the inspection.

topics.label: Inspection
topics.title: Locate the affected roofing
topics.description: Review observations around the covering, flashing, penetrations and drainage. Photographs can clarify the proposed repairs.

topics.label: Materials
topics.title: Check compatibility with the roof
topics.description: Ask which repair materials are proposed and how adjoining areas will be prepared. Discuss any need for further investigation.

topics.label: Replacement
topics.title: Consider broader work if needed
topics.description: Compare the replacement recommendation with the repair findings. Discuss the system and access with the property contact.

guide.title: Make repairs easy to locate
guide.copy: Ask for photographs and clear descriptions of the affected areas, materials and proposed work.
guide.secondCopy: Coordinate occupied areas and routes for materials and debris before repairs begin.

commercial-replacement.label: Commercial Roof Replacement
commercial-replacement.lead: Plan replacement with the proposed system, preparation, drainage and site access identified before installation.

topics.label: Existing roof
topics.title: Review condition and records
topics.description: Share known leaks, roof records and previous repairs. Ask which concealed conditions need assessment during preparation.

topics.label: System
topics.title: Name the selected products
topics.description: Discuss the system and its manufacturer documentation, including details around penetrations and adjoining roof areas.

topics.label: Drainage
topics.title: Coordinate edges and outlets
topics.description: Include gutters and downspouts in the proposal. New covering should not be assumed to resolve an existing drainage problem.

topics.label: Installation
topics.title: Plan with the property contact
topics.description: Discuss deliveries, access, occupant communication and cleanup. Confirm product and workmanship terms separately.

guide.title: Plan around the actual building
guide.copy: Review how the property operates and how installation can be coordinated with its use.
guide.secondCopy: Retain the estimate, system information, completed-work records and written coverage together.

commercial-types.label: Commercial Roof Systems
commercial-types.lead: Review the roof design and proposed system before comparing installation details and written coverage.

topics.label: Building
topics.title: Begin with the construction
topics.description: Discuss slope, access, penetrations and drainage. The system needs to suit the actual roof.

topics.label: System details
topics.title: Ask for named products
topics.description: Review manufacturer documents and details around seams, edges, penetrations and adjoining materials.

topics.label: Repairs
topics.title: Consider the existing condition
topics.description: An inspection establishes whether repair or replacement belongs in the discussion. Keep that decision separate from product comparisons.

topics.label: Drainage
topics.title: Include the outlets
topics.description: Review gutters, downspouts and existing drainage concerns alongside the roof covering.

guide.title: Compare complete proposals
guide.copy: Preparation and installation can differ along with products. Ask what is included behind each total.
guide.secondCopy: Manufacturer terms depend on selected products and installation. Review the actual written coverage.

local.label: Roofing & Exterior Services
local.lead: Choose roofing, siding, gutters and storm restoration with the materials and installation explained before work begins.

topics.label: Roofing
topics.title: Roof repair and replacement
topics.description: Inspect affected areas before deciding on repairs or broader replacement. Then compare the selected roof covering.

topics.label: Siding & gutters
topics.title: Plan adjoining exterior work
topics.description: Review siding, trim and drainage with the existing exterior. Ask what preparation and repairs are needed.

topics.label: Storm restoration
topics.title: Have reported damage inspected
topics.description: Share dates, safe photographs and new leaks. Roof King documents construction findings; your insurer determines coverage.

topics.label: More services
topics.title: Explore the rest of your exterior
topics.description: Decks, windows and attic insulation need different assessments. Bring the details of your property to the service conversation.

guide.title: Begin with the part needing work
guide.copy: A leak, damaged siding and an aging deck call for different inspections. Share what you have noticed before choosing the project.
guide.secondCopy: Ask which preparation, fastening and finishing are included and how additional repairs will be approved.

roofing-local.label: Residential Roofing Services
roofing-local.lead: Explore repair, replacement and products for your home, starting with the condition of the existing roof.

topics.label: Roof repair
topics.title: Find out what can be repaired
topics.description: Have leaks, missing shingles and flashing concerns inspected. The recommendation should identify affected areas and materials.

topics.label: Replacement
topics.title: Plan the whole installation
topics.description: Discuss removal, decking repairs, underlayment, flashing and selected covering. Review delivery, access and cleanup.

topics.label: GAF shingles
topics.title: Compare colors and specifications
topics.description: Browse genuine product images and explanations of classifications. Ask for samples and the written warranty proposed.

topics.label: Metal roofing
topics.title: Explore another covering
topics.description: Discuss panel style, finish, fastening and flashing. Compare the actual system and installation with shingle options.

guide.title: The visit starts with your roof
guide.copy: Share repairs, leaks and changes you have noticed. Establish the condition before choosing new products or replacement.
guide.secondTitle: Keep products in the product library
guide.secondCopy: Explore colors and specifications in one place, then return to what the inspection found on your home.

roof-cost.label: Roof Replacement Costs
roof-cost.lead: Understand the materials, preparation and repairs behind a roofing estimate before choosing a new roof.

topics.label: Roof & access
topics.title: Understand the work involved
topics.description: Area, pitch, layout and access affect replacement work. A final estimate needs an assessment of the property.

topics.label: Removal & repairs
topics.title: Account for preparation
topics.description: Review tear-off and how concealed decking repairs will be documented and approved. Ask what is included initially.

topics.label: Materials
topics.title: Compare exact products
topics.description: The covering, accessories, flashing and ventilation belong in the estimate. Use the library to narrow the choices.

topics.label: Planning tool
topics.title: Start with the roof calculator
topics.description: Roofr provides an initial planning tool. It does not replace an inspection or final written estimate.

guide.title: Read the items behind the total
guide.copy: Review named materials, preparation, installation and cleanup. Ask about exclusions and how further repairs are approved.
guide.secondTitle: Products do not establish a final price
guide.secondCopy: The library helps with styles and specifications. Roof condition and installation still need assessment.

siding-cost.label: Siding Replacement Costs
siding-cost.lead: See what belongs in an estimate, from removal and wall preparation to panels, trim and finishing.

topics.label: Walls & details
topics.title: Consider the exterior layout
topics.description: Area, openings, corners and trim affect the work. An estimate should reflect the actual house.

topics.label: Existing walls
topics.title: Plan removal and preparation
topics.description: Discuss concealed wall damage and how repairs discovered during removal will be approved.

topics.label: Materials
topics.title: Name the selected siding
topics.description: Compare material, product line, profile, color and trim. A brand name alone does not identify the proposed exterior.

topics.label: Complete estimate
topics.title: Include finishing and cleanup
topics.description: Review flashing, trim, fastening and debris removal. Discuss financing terms separately from the construction.

guide.title: The panel price is one part
guide.copy: Preparation, trim, flashing and repairs affect the finished installation. Ask about each alongside the main siding.
guide.secondCopy: Compare siding and trim outdoors with the roof and masonry, then confirm the exact choices in writing.

gutter-cost.label: Gutter Replacement Costs
gutter-cost.lead: Understand how lengths, sizes, outlets, downspouts and adjoining repairs shape a replacement estimate.

topics.label: Layout
topics.title: Count the drainage details
topics.description: Review lengths, corners, outlets and downspouts. Ask how the proposal addresses observed overflow or drainage concerns.

topics.label: Fascia
topics.title: Include preparation and repairs
topics.description: Review the attachment surface and how fascia repairs will be identified and approved.

topics.label: Protection
topics.title: Identify optional products
topics.description: Ask for the exact guard or support system. Review compatibility, maintenance and coverage rather than treating all guards alike.

topics.label: Installation
topics.title: Review removal and fastening
topics.description: Identify new gutters, downspouts and old material removal. Discuss access and cleanup before scheduling.

guide.title: Follow the drainage layout
guide.copy: Ask where water leaves the roofline and how new gutters address the concern, as well as how much gutter is included.
guide.secondCopy: Review guards or supports separately from necessary gutter and fascia repairs.

commercial-gutters.label: Commercial Gutters
commercial-gutters.lead: Review commercial gutters around building drainage, attachment points and access.

topics.label: Drainage layout
topics.title: Show us where water overflows
topics.description: Review gutters, outlets and downspouts before choosing replacement materials.
topics.detail: Discuss proposed sizes, fastening and discharge arrangements alongside the problems you have noticed.

topics.label: Seamless gutters
topics.title: Plan the roofline details
topics.description: A seamless installation still needs clear corners, outlet and downspout connections.
topics.detail: Review fascia condition and any repairs required before the gutters attach.

topics.label: Gutter guards
topics.title: Compare protection with the system
topics.description: Guards and continuous hangers have different functions. Review the exact product and its compatibility.
topics.detail: Protection does not correct damaged or undersized gutters. Ask about cleaning and inspection.

topics.label: Roof edges
topics.title: Include adjoining repairs
topics.description: Gutter work connects with fascia and roofing details. Discuss damage in those areas as part of the proposal.
topics.detail: If roof repairs are also needed, ask how the work will be coordinated.

guide.title: Follow the water through the estimate
guide.copy: Discuss where water enters the gutters, how it reaches downspouts and where it is discharged. The proposal should explain that route.
guide.secondCopy: Discuss occupied areas, delivery routes and access restrictions before work begins. Agree on who will communicate with the installation team.

commercial-siding.label: Commercial Siding
commercial-siding.lead: Plan building siding around wall condition, selected materials and installation access.

topics.label: Wall condition
topics.title: Inspect before choosing the work
topics.description: Share loose panels, moisture concerns and previous repairs with the team.
topics.detail: Ask how removal and any concealed wall repairs will be documented.

topics.label: Choose materials
topics.title: Find the right siding profile
topics.description: Compare vinyl, engineered wood and fiber cement, including care requirements for the exact product.
topics.detail: Judge samples outdoors beside your roofing, masonry and trim.

topics.label: Trim & flashing
topics.title: Plan the whole wall appearance
topics.description: Window surrounds, corners and material transitions belong with the main panels.
topics.detail: Discuss fastening, flashing and finishing requirements for the selected product.

topics.label: Installation
topics.title: Prepare for removal and delivery
topics.description: Review access, deliveries and protection of surrounding areas before scheduling.
topics.detail: The estimate should identify products and preparation, with a way to approve additional work.

guide.title: New siding should feel coordinated
guide.copy: Plan trim widths, corners and accent profiles with the main siding, roof and masonry before ordering materials.
guide.secondCopy: Discuss occupied areas, delivery routes and access restrictions before work begins. Agree on who will communicate with the installation team.

commercial-storm.label: Commercial Storm Restoration
commercial-storm.lead: Document reported damage to the building roof and exterior, then review repairs with the property contact.

topics.label: Hail damage
topics.title: Have suspected damage inspected
topics.description: Changes in shingles and surrounding metalwork can prompt an inspection. Ground photographs alone do not establish the extent of roof damage.
topics.detail: Share the storm date and new leaks. Ask for the findings and recommended repairs in writing.

topics.label: Wind damage
topics.title: Review missing or displaced materials
topics.description: Photograph visible changes from a safe ground-level position and keep clear of loose materials.
topics.detail: An inspection can review shingles, roof edges and related exterior damage before repairs are recommended.

topics.label: Ice damage
topics.title: Discuss roof-edge ice and water entry
topics.description: Tell our team where ice has formed and whether water is entering the building.
topics.detail: Stay off icy roofing and discuss the removal approach rather than striking roofing materials.

topics.label: Documentation
topics.title: Keep photographs and findings together
topics.description: Keep storm dates, photographs and previous roof records for the inspection.
topics.detail: Roof King can document construction findings. Your insurer determines policy coverage and claim decisions.

guide.title: Separate observations from repair recommendations
guide.copy: Ask what was found on the roof, siding and gutters, and why each repair is recommended. Not every visible mark calls for the same work.
guide.secondCopy: Discuss occupied areas, delivery routes and access restrictions before work begins. Agree on who will communicate with the installation team.

calculator.label: Roofing Estimate Calculator
calculator.lead: Use Roof King’s Roofr estimator to start planning, then review actual roof condition and installation with our team.

topics.title: Understand the work involved
topics.description: Area, pitch, layout and access affect replacement work. A final estimate needs an assessment of the property.

topics.description: Review tear-off and how concealed decking repairs will be documented and approved. Ask what is included initially.

topics.title: Compare exact products
topics.description: The covering, accessories, flashing and ventilation belong in the estimate. Use the library to narrow the choices.

topics.title: Start with the roof calculator
topics.description: Roofr provides an initial planning tool. It does not replace an inspection or final written estimate.
